title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference | Week 3 vs. San Francisco 49ers
headline: Will Johnson is likely headed to season-ending IR, and Marvin Harrison Jr. is improving as a run blocker, per LaFleur.
summary: LaFleur said the team is turning the page from Sunday's loss and focusing on a San Francisco 49ers defense he called very good. He said the run game is a work in progress, with some areas solid and others needing major improvement, and pointed to better play-calling and clarity as fixes. On injuries, he said Will Johnson was placed on IR and is likely out for the season, with a neck issue the medical staff wants to protect, so the team is bracing for that. He said Tip is progressing day to day. He praised Marvin Harrison Jr.'s effort as a blocker, saying he has gotten better and embraced the challenge, and said Harrison is in a good place mentally despite outside narrative. On the 49ers, LaFleur described Raheem Morris's defense as having new faces and similarities to his Atlanta units, with only about two games of sample size. He also commented on Paris Johnson's accountability after the game and said the offensive line needs to keep raising its standard.

title: Kevin Stefanski on Atlanta Falcons preparation for Green Bay Packers matchup | Press Conference
headline: Penix's return from injury is on track but the Week 3 starting job isn't officially confirmed; AJ Terrell is out Thursday and Tua Tagovailoa's backup role is undecided.
summary: Stefanski said preparation for the Thursday night game at Green Bay is going well, with the team traveling later in the day and working through a condensed short-week schedule. He described daily check-ins with Michael Penix Jr. on his recovery and said Penix knows his body best, with the staff judging he is ready after a hard workout. He pushed back on the idea that Week 3 was always the planned return, saying decisions are day-to-day based on new information and medical input. He did not confirm Penix as the starter and declined to say whether the team would be dealing with a post-game rest plan. On injuries, he said the injury report will come after the walkthrough, since short weeks mean players don't practice in a way that clarifies status. He said losing AJ Terrell is tough, that the time away should help him get healthy for the long haul, and that other players will step up. Tua Tagovailoa was fully back in practice, is trending in the right direction, and his backup role is still to be determined. On the Packers, he praised Matt LaFleur and defensive coordinator John Gannon and called Green Bay well coached with good players at every level. He also discussed linebacker length, praised Divine Deablo for playing through illness Sunday, and explained the team's rush-plan philosophy.

title: Joe Brady Reflects On 2-0 Start, Looks Ahead To Facing The Los Angeles Chargers, And More

He credited DL Deone Walker's jump to an outstanding offseason and a scheme that fits him, while stressing that consistency across games still needs to be shown. On defense, he said there is no single issue, only several "smoke detectors" to clean up from Week 2 to Week 3, mainly trusting technique and the scheme and getting off the field on third down. He said the offense's struggles are about getting out of behind-the-chains situations. He rejected the idea that Moore's absence changed the passing approach, pointing to Josh Palmer's explosive downfield plays. Brady praised DL DeWayne Carter's return from his Achilles injury and expanded role after Ed Oliver went down, and called OLB Greg Rousseau's play high-level. He also said the Bills' finish-and-win mentality has been encouraging, and he gave Chargers QB Justin Herbert and Mike McDaniel's offense respect, noting their run defense has been strong.

Jonathon Brooks had a significant groin injury; after multiple opinions, he will have surgery, with a similar return timeline to a non-surgical route, and he is going on IR to open a roster spot. summary: Case Keenum, the backup quarterback, spoke Wednesday at Halas Hall and said he feels very prepared to play if called upon this week. title: Todd Monken Press Conference : September 23rd, 2026
headline: Monken says the run game and short-yardage package need work against Carolina, Deshaun Watson is still rebuilding after a long layoff, and Blake Whiteheart's go-ahead touchdown was a bright spot.
summary: Monken opened by saying he expects a strong home crowd and that the team wants to make it hard on Carolina this Sunday after two road games. He said the running game is not sustainable at its current level and blamed scheming, coaching, and execution equally, with the staff included. He called the short-yardage sneak package not ready and said the coaches must coach it better. On Deshaun Watson, he said Watson's legs have helped on third downs and that read-option and RPO looks vary by game plan. He clarified that calling Watson "young" meant limited recent game and practice reps after injury, not his age. He said Watson has worked about 22 months to return and should be allowed to play freely. He praised Blake Whiteheart's catch-and-run touchdown, calling him one of the hardest workers and comparing his work ethic to Brock Bowers. Monken also previewed Carolina's Bryce Young, whom he called hard to contain, and said the Thursday game against Pittsburgh on a short week will shape how the staff schedules preparation.

Asked about Michael Pittman, he said the trainer has a plan for every player evaluated that morning, Pittman will work in practice, and the result will show on the injury report. He praised Jamel Dean and Asante Samuel Jr. for playing at a high level, especially in the big-play department, which the staff is focused on. He said Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington are a big part of the game plan each week, and that he'd like to see them catch more passes, even though the team throws about 80 times in two games. He called DK Metcalf a professional with no concern about his work ethic or connection with Aaron Rodgers. McCarthy said the offense needs to hit all areas of the field and get its shot plays off the call sheet, and that third-down struggles are about execution rather than the play calls. He called Cincinnati's rebuilt defensive front a large, challenging group with a strong start.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Previews Week 3 vs. Commanders
headline: Emmanwori's workload is climbing in his return, Darnold's Week 3 status is a Friday decision, and Anthony Bradford heads to IR with a hoped-for full recovery.
summary: Macdonald said this is the Seahawks' first normal seven-day week of the season, with a 10 a.m. Pacific kickoff on the East Coast and a focus on being decisive in the process. He said it is still early for judging schemes and that teams can run almost anything, so he will not reveal much about the new coordinators yet. On Nick Emmanwori, he said the staff is being deliberate about his reps because of his return, but his workload will be significantly higher and he will be on the field a good amount. Quarterback Sam Darnold will practice but won't take every rep today, with the workload ramping up through the week, and the team will decide on his availability before Friday ends. Macdonald praised Rodney Thomas II as the player the staff expected, and said Dante Fowler's pass-rush movement and personality have stood out in his limited snaps. Anthony Bradford is going on IR, which Macdonald called unfortunate but expects him to fully recover from, and he sounded encouraged by how Christian Haynes and a rookie filled in. Macdonald also addressed a released video of a mic'd-up conversation with Sean, apologizing and taking responsibility for it. He praised the offense's strong start and said there is still room to grow, and he discussed Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough and their quarterback situation.

summary: Shanahan opened with a practice report: Mike Evans (hip), Demarcus Robinson (ankle), and Romello Height (hand) did not practice, while Nick Bosa, Dre Greenlaw, Christian McCaffrey, and Trent Williams were on veteran days. On the defensive line, he said losing depth at tackle is a concern, so the team signed one player and added three practice-squad players to compete for spots. He said the team may place several injured players on IR, but decisions are still being balanced. He praised Brandin Cooks as a veteran who will need to learn the offense and earn a spot in the top five receivers, with special teams playing a major role in that decision. On the Cardinals, he said they are well-coached, similar schematically to the Rams, and have more talent than people credit. He credited Brock Purdy's consistency, accuracy, and coachability, and said Connor Colby has been most consistent in these first two games. Asked about the defensive end rotation, he named Nelson, Muhammad and Walker as three options and said it is too early to know who will start. Jacob Parrish was full in practice after being limited last week. Bowles praised David Walker's sack but said he still needs to improve his defensive fundamentals. He expects no major starter changes, though some adjustments will show up later in the week. On the Vikings, he called Kevin O'Connell's offense smart and complementary, described Brian Flores' defense as disguise-heavy, and said Kyler Murray is a strong arm with the mobility to be a real threat. He said the team must get off blocks and tackle better, and win the turnover battle. He defended Baker Mayfield, saying the problems start with the coaches and that the offense must call plays and execute better. He said Bucky Irving's running could be a major part of the Sunday game plan, and that Jalen McMillan's seven snaps were a planned build-up that could grow if he progresses.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Pollard (ankle soreness) sat out Wednesday's practice, James Williams is full, and Cam Ward is praised for ball security as the Titans prep for the Giants.
summary: Saleh opened by saying Tony Pollard is dealing with ankle soreness and will be out today, while James Williams is full. He called Giants QB Jameis Winston a dangerous, talented passer who can change a game quickly, and said the Titans respect him without changing their defensive approach. On kickoffs, Saleh said the unit must improve on returns and coverage, praised Joey's dirty-ball kickoffs, and said the team always wants to force returns. He said Anthony Hill is still a young rookie who will keep improving, and called Jeffery Simmons a special player who has been very effective in pass rush wins. Saleh said the Week 2 loss came down to late-game detail and one-on-one execution, and that the young players must keep learning. He praised Dennard Wilson's defense and Cam Ward's ball security, saying turnovers are a key indicator of wins. He said Cody Barton has done well alongside the other linebackers. On Wan'Dale Robinson, he said his production depends on game flow and opportunity on third down. He expects the Giants to come out aggressive after their short-week setbacks.
